content.value_statement: Distributed systems fail when service boundaries, contracts, and operations are unclear. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan microservices with events, APIs, resilience, and migration steps.
actual_capabilities: Maps service boundaries and ownership from business capabilities.
Compares REST, gRPC, GraphQL, events, queues, and pub/sub communication.
Explains data ownership, database-per-service, saga, and compensation patterns.
Provides API gateway, service client, event bus, saga, and circuit breaker examples.
Defines migration steps and operational guardrails for decomposing monoliths.
limitations: Does not deploy services or provision infrastructure by itself.
Example snippets require adaptation, security review, and production testing.
Assumes the team can operate distributed systems and observability.
Not ideal for small systems that fit a modular monolith.

use_cases.title: Decompose a Monolith
use_cases.description: Identify bounded contexts, data ownership, and migration stages for extracting services without breaking core workflows.

use_cases.title: Design Service Communication
use_cases.description: Choose synchronous APIs, asynchronous events, or queues based on latency, consistency, and coupling needs.

use_cases.title: Plan Resilient Workflows
use_cases.description: Add circuit breakers, retries, sagas, and compensation steps for distributed business processes.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new distributed system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product domain and propose service boundaries. Include each service owner, main data objects, public contracts, and reasons for each boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Communication Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate architecture design for multiple services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these services and workflows, recommend when to use REST, events, queues, or gRPC. Explain tradeoffs for latency, consistency, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Saga Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a saga for this business process. List each step, required data, failure cases, compensation actions, and observability signals.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Migration Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before extracting services from a monolith.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this microservices migration plan. Identify risky boundaries, shared data problems, operational gaps, rollout sequence issues, and safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: A retail monolith has checkout, payment, inventory, and fulfillment logic in one application.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose service boundaries, ownership rules, event flows, and a staged extraction plan with rollback points.

output_examples.input: A payment dependency causes order creation to fail during brief outages.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, fallback behavior, and monitoring for partial failures.

output_examples.input: A team wants microservices for a small prototype with limited operational support.
output_examples.output: The skill would explain why a modular monolith may be safer until ownership, deployment, and observability maturity improve.

best_practices: Start from business capabilities and clear ownership before choosing infrastructure.
Prefer asynchronous events for workflows that do not need immediate consistency.
Define contracts, health checks, tracing, and rollback plans before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Starting with microservices when a modular monolith would meet the need.
Sharing one database across services and calling it independent ownership.
Making every workflow synchronous and ignoring network failure modes.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design service boundaries, communication patterns, data ownership, sagas, and resilience patterns for microservices.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready services?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that need engineering review, implementation, and testing.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when a modular monolith is simpler or when the team cannot operate distributed systems.

faq.question: Does it support event-driven architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Kafka-style event publishing, subscriptions, pub/sub patterns, and eventual consistency tradeoffs.

faq.question: Does it cover distributed transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains saga orchestration, compensating actions, failure handling, and transaction workflow design.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex.
